findings.title: JWT algorithm confusion: HS256 verified using RSA public key as HMAC secret
findings.attack_path: Attacker fetches the public JWKS at /identity/api/auth/jwks.json, base64-encodes the RSA public key, then forges an HS256 token signing it with that public key as the HMAC secret. validateJwtToken() in JwtProvider.java derives the HMAC secret from the public key for HS256 tokens, so the forged token verifies as any user/role including ADMIN.

findings.title: JWT verification accepts alg=none (PlainJWT) and attacker-controlled jku/kid keys
findings.attack_path: validateJwtToken() falls back to PlainJWT.parse() and returns true for unsigned (alg=none) tokens, and getKeyFromJkuHeader() loads a JWKS from an attacker-supplied jku URL (also an SSRF), while a kid containing /dev/null forces a known 'AA==' secret. Any of these lets an attacker mint a fully trusted token as admin.

findings.title: RSA private signing key committed to source control and shipped in images
findings.attack_path: services/identity/jwks.json (and the copies under deploy/*/keys/jwks.json) contains the full RSA key including private components (d, p, q). Anyone with repository or image read access extracts the private key and signs valid JWTs for any account, defeating all token-based auth across every service.

findings.title: Unauthenticated/permitAll endpoints expose dashboard PII and issue API keys
findings.attack_path: WebSecurityConfig.java marks /identity/api/v2/user/dashboard and /identity/management/user/** as permitAll. The dashboard returns user profile, available credit and identifiers, and /management/user/apikey issues a non-expiring API key (generateApiKey has no expiration claim). The same broken function-level authorization pattern exposes the workshop admin listing /workshop/api/management/users/all (E20, AdminUserView) to non-admins, enabling unauthenticated data harvest and durable credential minting.

findings.title: OTP password reset has no attempt limit on /v2/check-otp with a 4-digit OTP
findings.attack_path: AuthController /v2/check-otp calls otpService.validateOtp(), which (unlike secureValidateOtp) never caps otp.count. With a 4-digit OTP (10000 values) an attacker brute-forces the reset code for any known email and takes over the account; the secure v3 variant that caps at 9 attempts is not wired to v2.

findings.title: Predictable OTP and email-change tokens generated with Math.random()
findings.attack_path: OTPGenerator.generateRandom and EmailTokenGenerator.generateRandom both use Math.random() (non-cryptographic PRNG) instead of SecureRandom. An attacker who observes or models the PRNG state can predict reset OTPs and email-change tokens, then use /login-with-token to authenticate as the victim without their password.

findings.title: BOLA: vehicle location retrievable by any car UUID without ownership check
findings.attack_path: VehicleController.getLocationBOLA(@PathVariable carId) returns vehicleService.getVehicleLocation(carId) with no check that the authenticated caller owns carId. An authenticated user enumerates/guesses car UUIDs to track other users' vehicle locations.

findings.title: OS command injection in profile video convert_video conversion params
findings.attack_path: When ENABLE_SHELL_INJECTION=true, ProfileServiceImpl.convertVideo() string-formats the stored conversion_params into 'convertVideo -i %s %s' and runs it via BashCommand.executeBashCommand(), giving arbitrary command execution in the identity container. Likelihood is gated by the (deliberately) optional flag.

findings.title: BFLA: any user can delete any profile video via admin endpoint
findings.attack_path: DELETE /identity/api/v2/admin/videos/{video_id} (deleteVideoBOLA) performs an admin-style delete keyed only on video_id with no role gate, so a normal user deletes other users' videos.

findings.title: NoSQL operator injection in community validate-coupon
findings.attack_path: ValidateCoupon unmarshals the raw request body straight into a bson.M and passes it to models.ValidateCode as the Mongo filter. Sending {"coupon_code":{"$gt":""}} or {"$where":...} lets the attacker bypass the intended exact-match and dump/abuse coupon documents.

findings.title: SQL injection in workshop apply_coupon raw query
findings.attack_path: ApplyCouponView concatenates coupon_request_body['coupon_code'] directly into a raw SELECT against applied_coupon via cursor.execute(). A crafted coupon_code injects SQL to read/modify arbitrary Postgres data (users, orders, credit) in the shared crapi database.

findings.title: Business-logic abuse: client controls credit amount and refund on apply_coupon / order update
findings.attack_path: ApplyCouponView adds the attacker-supplied 'amount' to available_credit, and OrderControlView.put credits the order total back whenever 'status' is flipped to returned/refund. Both let a user inflate their store credit arbitrarily (financial fraud).

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery via merchant contact_mechanic mechanic_api URL
findings.attack_path: ContactMechanicView issues requests.get(request_data['mechanic_api'], verify=False) to a fully attacker-controlled URL, forwarding the caller's Authorization header. The attacker pivots to internal-only services (identity, gateway, cloud metadata) and exfiltrates responses; repeat_request_if_failed up to 100 also amplifies it into a DoS/port-scan primitive.

findings.title: Unauthenticated BOLA on merchant service_requests by VIN
findings.attack_path: UserServiceRequestsView.get has no @jwt_auth_required decorator and filters service requests only by the path VIN with no ownership check, exposing any vehicle's service history (incl. owner-linked data) to anyone who knows/guesses a VIN.

findings.title: Unauthenticated BOLA on shop order detail leaking payment/card data
findings.attack_path: OrderControlView.get fetches Order.objects.get(id=order_id) with no @jwt_auth_required and no owner check, returns the order plus payment info (card_number/owner/type from the gateway). Sequential order IDs let an attacker harvest other customers' orders and partial card data.

findings.title: Privilege self-assignment via mechanic signup
findings.attack_path: SignUpView creates a User with role MECH using only a client-submitted mechanic_code and no verification that the code is authorized, letting any actor self-provision a mechanic account and reach mechanic-only service-request functionality.

findings.title: MCP server authentication bypass when Authorization header is absent
findings.attack_path: MCPAuthMiddleware only validates credentials when an Authorization header is present ('if not auth_header: await self.app(...); return'). Any request with no header passes straight through unauthenticated to the MCP tool surface (port 5500 is published), so tools run without credentials.

findings.title: MCP debug_web_service tool enables SSRF/path traversal into web /debug surface
findings.attack_path: The MCP tool debug_web_service does client.get(f'/debug/{path}') with no validation, and the web nginx serves /debug as a static alias including access.log. An attacker (or an injected prompt steering the agent) reads debug artifacts and access logs, which leak tokens, emails and request bodies.

findings.title: Over-permissioned LLM agent (terminal/SQL/MCP tools) with prompt-injection exposure
findings.attack_path: build_langgraph_agent attaches a SQLDatabaseToolkit (direct Postgres query tools), MCP tools, and a system prompt that tells the model to use terminal/code_interpreter/browser/file_manager and 'simulate exploitation'. Untrusted content reaches the model via posts/comments (E13) and search titles surfaced by the get_latest_post_on_topic MCP tool (E12), so an indirect prompt injection can drive the SQL/terminal tools to read or modify the shared databases on behalf of the attacker.

findings.title: Indirect prompt injection / data leak: MCP tool posts user context into public forum
findings.attack_path: get_latest_post_on_topic fetches the admin dashboard with the service ApiKey and posts the full user_info as a comment on the latest community post, and reflects an unsanitized search title back. This leaks privileged context into a public, attacker-readable store and provides a stored-content channel to feed further prompt injection into the agent.

findings.title: Hardcoded credentials throughout: DB, JWT secret, gateway basic auth, admin API user
findings.attack_path: checkCreds() hardcodes vendorcrapi/Pa$$4Vendor_1 for the dealership gateway; docker-compose and k8s configs hardcode DB_PASSWORD=crapisecretpassword, JWT_SECRET=crapi, keystore passw0rd, and chatbot API_USER admin@example.com / API_PASSWORD Admin!123. Anyone reading the repo/images reuses these to access the gateway's SSN/card data and the shared databases.

findings.title: Service-to-service TLS verification disabled (InsecureSkipVerify / verify=False)
findings.attack_path: community auth/token.go sets TLSClientConfig InsecureSkipVerify:true and both workshop utils/jwt.py and merchant views pass verify=False on calls to the identity verify endpoint and external URLs. An on-path attacker on the internal network can MITM token-verification and SSRF traffic without certificate errors.

findings.title: Token verification relies on unsigned claim parsing in callers (ParseUnverified / verify_signature False)
findings.attack_path: community ExtractTokenID uses jwt.ParseUnverified to read claims and workshop jwt_auth_required decodes with verify_signature:False, both trusting identity's /auth/verify for signature checking. Because identity's validateJwtToken (TM-001/002) accepts forged/none/jku tokens, every downstream service inherits the broken trust decision and the deprecated dgrijalva/jwt-go lib compounds the risk.

findings.title: Permissive CORS (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) on authenticated APIs
findings.attack_path: community middlewares.go sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin:* with Authorization allowed on every route. Combined with bearer tokens passed via query param/header, a malicious site can drive cross-origin reads of community data on behalf of a logged-in victim.

findings.title: Debug surfaces exposed: Django DEBUG via LOG_LEVEL, Go pprof, nginx /debug access logs
findings.attack_path: settings.py flips DEBUG=True when LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG with ALLOWED_HOSTS=['*'] (stack traces/SQL leak); community mounts net/http/pprof under /debug/pprof when DEBUG=1; nginx serves /debug/ as a static alias and writes access.log there. Together they leak source paths, request bodies, tokens and runtime internals to unauthenticated callers.

findings.title: Self-hosted TLS private keys and weak keystore passwords committed to repo
findings.attack_path: Every service ships its server.key/server.crt (and identity a server.p12 with password passw0rd) in version control. An attacker who has the repo or any image holds the TLS private keys and can impersonate services or decrypt/MITM TLS sessions where these certs are trusted.

findings.title: CI/CD image build & publish pipeline as unguarded supply-chain boundary
findings.attack_path: publish.yml / workflow-multiarch.yml build and push crapi/* images consumed by every deployment; floating tags (e.g. chromadb/chroma:latest, :${VERSION:-latest}) and committed registry/build scripts mean a compromised pipeline, dependency, or base image silently ships to all runtime services.

findings.title: Unrestricted resource consumption: no rate limiting on auth/search/agent endpoints
findings.attack_path: No throttling exists on /v2/check-otp (enables the OTP brute force in TM-005), on the LLM /ask endpoint (each call spins up an agent that can run many tool/LLM requests, driving provider cost and load), or on contact_mechanic's repeat loop (up to 100 outbound requests). An attacker exhausts compute, money, and the small per-service CPU/memory limits set in docker-compose.

findings.title: Captured emails (OTP/reset/email-change tokens) exposed via /mailhog proxy
findings.attack_path: nginx proxies /mailhog/ to the mailhog web UI, which stores all outbound mail (including password-reset OTPs and email-change tokens) in MongoDB with no authentication. An attacker who reaches the mailhog UI reads other users' reset codes/tokens and completes account takeover via /login-with-token.
